_comment: Budgets checked by scripts/perf_check.py on every PR. Timings are LibreOffice on a CI runner, with roughly 3x headroom over local runs. edit_recalc_s is a duration edit near the top of the plan. OFFSET is allowed only in Tasks, for reading another row's calculated value (predecessor drivers, parent WBS, and the critical path's successor look-ups) (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Raise a budget only with a reason in the PR; never to hide a regression. v1.3 raised formulas_max (sample 30,000 -> 35,000, stress 125,000 -> 150,000) for earned value and the report lists: 18 Tasks columns (one formula per task each) and about 960 report cells; the edit time rose by 0.06 s at 1,000 tasks. Reports 2 raised the sample formulas_max to 38,000 for the Resource Report's weekly grids (3 grids x 25 resources x 26-27 weeks; blank resource rows cost almost nothing to calculate) and the agile columns; one edit rose by about 0.02 s on the sample and 0.1 s at 1,000 tasks. Reports 3 raised the stress formulas_max to 155,000 for the RAID, Decisions, Changes and History sheets (about 1,200 formulas, fixed: they don't grow with the task count); edit time unchanged. Leave (v1.4) raised the sample formulas_max to 41,000: two leave grids (25 resources x 26 weeks / sprints), their row and month-column helpers, and the Over-allocated column on Tasks. The leave grids read inputs only, so editing a task doesn't recalculate them. v1.5 (four predecessors, all constraint types) raised formulas_max (sample 41,000 -> 44,000, stress 155,000 -> 172,000) and the OFFSET allow-list (sample 1,400 -> 2,200, stress 7,000 -> 11,000): links 3-4 add 12 helper columns (position, problem, plan / forecast driver, finish / slack key each; 4 of them the OFFSET drivers), constraints add 4 and As Late As Possible 5, while the predecessor text helpers went (-4): 17 Tasks columns, one formula per task each. One edit rose by about 0.002 s on the sample and 0.06 s at 1,000 tasks; full recalculation is unchanged. Assignments (v1.5, several people per task) raised formulas_max (sample 44,000 -> 47,000, stress 172,000 -> 180,000): the Assignments sheet (17 formulas per row: 100 rows on the sample, 132 at 1,000 tasks) and 4 Tasks columns (total work and cost, the first person's actual cost, Resource Names). Per-resource sums gained one SUMIFS over the Assignments sheet each. One edit rose by about 0.01 s on the sample and was unchanged at 1,000 tasks. v1.7 text inputs (B-905 Predecessors, B-906 Resources: one cell each instead of 12 link inputs, Resource / Units and the Assignments sheet) raised formulas_max (sample 47,000 -> 50,000, stress 180,000 -> 200,000) and the stress full_recalc_s_max (2.5 -> 3.5 s): each cell is split by formulas into hidden per-link and per-person columns (44 per task), and per-resource totals sum one SUMIFS per person slot that a plan uses (MaxPeople). Measured at 1,000 tasks: full 1.36 -> 2.3 s, one edit 0.82 -> 1.2 s; sample: full 0.31 -> 0.38 s, one edit 0.10 -> 0.16 s. The Assignments-sheet design was faster (its sums scanned ~130 rows, not 1,000 per slot) but needed a second sheet and three inputs per extra person; the one-cell design is what the owner asked for and stays inside every edit budget.
